entries.topic: Ancestors the texts themselves name: Hobbes, Hoppe, Austrian school, Carlyle, Burnham, Frederick the Great

claims.text: 'Moldbug on Carlyle' (2010, 82 pp.) compiles three UR essays: 'From Mises to Carlyle: My Sick Journey to the Dark Side of the Force' (February 2010) and 'Why Carlyle Matters' and 'Carlyle in the 20th Century: Fascism and Socialism' (consecutive weeks, July 2009)

Tait: writings of Carlyle, Burnham and Hoppe, which 'variously proposed the failure of democracy', prompted Yarvin's turn; Glenn Reynolds introduced him to Mises and Rothbard; neocameralism based on Frederick the Great's cameralism (Gray, Atlantic 2017)

Land: Moldbug's 'formative influences are Austro-libertarian, but that's all over'; current 'From Thomas Hobbes to Hans-Hermann Hoppe'; Frederick the Great as closest historical equivalent of neocameralism (pp. 3–6)
A 2009 Yarvin post said 'the innate character and intelligence of some is more suited to mastery than slavery' and that this is 'most parsimoniously explained by genetic differences'

Democracy: The God That Failed (Transaction, 2001): monarchy as 'privately-owned government' preferable to democracy, both inferior to a 'natural order'/private law society; Kofman (New Yorker 2025) credits it with pushing Yarvin toward monarchism; Julian Waller: 'such a direct influence that it's kind of obscene'
Burnham, The Managerial Revolution (1941): managers, not capitalists or workers, becoming the new ruling class; The Machiavellians (1943)

Media Matters quotes Yarvin's 2009 post 'Why Carlyle Matters': 'Not all humans are born the same, of course' ... 'the innate character and intelligence of some is more suited to mastery than slavery. For others, it is more suited to slavery.' 'A person makes a good slave if he is loyal, patient, and not exceptionally bright or stubborn.' 'This broad pattern of observation is most parsimoniously explained by genetic differences.'

entries.topic: Technocracy Inc., Howard Scott, energy certificates, the Technate; Joshua N. Haldeman; Musk's own statements

claims.text: Scott founded Technocracy Inc. (with M. King Hubbert, 1933); proposed replacing the price system with energy accounting; engineers to run a continental 'technate'; overstated credentials

Energy certificates: scrip equal to the energy used in a year, distributed equally, worthless if not used within the year; membership may have reached a quarter-million in early 1933; Columbia distanced itself after Scott's 13 January 1933 Hotel Pierre speech
The Technate was to merge Canada, Greenland, Mexico, the US and parts of Central America; Townley: Musk's market approach and the administration's retention of money and wages differ from Technocracy

Haldeman (1902–1974): in Technocracy Inc. 1936–1941; arrested 8 October 1940 under the Defence of Canada Regulations; fined $200 in Regina on 23 October 1940 over 'Statement of Patriotism by Those Who Were Technocrats'

CBC: Haldeman led Social Credit in Saskatchewan (1945) and chaired its national council (1946); defended publication of the Protocols of the Elders of Zion, saying whether it was fraudulent 'is not the point'; moved to Pretoria in 1950; wrote in 1951 that South Africa's government 'knows how to handle the native question'; died 13 January 1974
CBC: Musk's quoted remarks about his grandfather concern adventure ('desire for adventure, exploration'); none about technocracy
Lepore (opinion): many of Musk's ideas 'resemble those championed by' his grandfather; Haldeman technocrat No. 10450-1; Scott: the movement 'has no theory for the assumption of power'
Musk posted 'Accelerating Starship development to build the Martian Technocracy' in June 2019, without explanation
Musk, 2 June 2016: government on Mars 'Most likely ... would be a direct democracy, not representative'
Musk, 11 Feb 2025: 'We don't live in a democracy. We live in a bureaucracy'; if the bureaucracy is in charge, 'what meaning does democracy actually have?'

CBC: Haldeman born in a log cabin in Minnesota in 1902; finished chiropractic training 1926; lost his farm in the 1930s when unable to keep up loan payments; left Technocracy after it shifted to backing 'complete economic and military collaboration with Soviet Russia'; in The International Conspiracy in Health (mid-1960s) wrote of an 'Invisible Government' carrying out 'the International Conspiracy'; died in a plane crash in 1974; Musk told Ashlee Vance (2015 book): 'My grandfather had this desire for adventure, exploration — doing crazy things.'

entries.topic: Libertarian exit (Seasteading, Friedman, Thiel 2009), Hoppe and the Austrian school, disputes over lineage

claims.text: Thiel, 13 April 2009: 'I no longer believe that freedom and democracy are compatible'; named 1920 extension of the franchise to women and welfare growth; three frontiers cyberspace, outer space, seasteading; 'escape from politics in all its forms'; follow-up of 1 May 2009: 'Voting is not under siege in America, but many other rights are'
Seasteading Institute founded 15 April 2008 by Wayne Gramlich and Patri Friedman; Thiel $500,000 seed (Wired, 18 May 2008); French Polynesia MoU 13 January 2017, declared lapsed at end of 2017
Thiel's giving to TSI: $1.25 million (2011 report; TSI said he does not 'dictate' plans) and $1.7 million (Business Insider 2018; left board 2011; later called seasteading 'not quite feasible')

Hoppe (2025): 'I do not follow Yarvin's writings closely – too much rambling for my taste'; met him once at a Thiel-invited gathering; ideal 'thousands upon thousands of Liechtensteins'; separates his view from the 'Silicon valley crowd' model of running the state like a business

Hoppe, Democracy: The God That Failed (2001), pp. 216–218: 'There can be no tolerance toward democrats and communists in a libertarian social order'; Rothbard his 'principal teacher'; UNLV 1986–2008; Property and Freedom Society 2006
Haider: Land reads Thiel's escape from politics through Hirschman's voice and exit; Land's provisional example of exit is white flight
